source: Analyst's Notebook MER traverse map service, layers 1stSolPnts and merATraverse
citation: Spirit traverse. Data NASA / JPL-Caltech / MER science team, compiled and published by azmth.space, https://azmth.space/mars/data
compilation: Compiled by azmth.space: the published layers joined into one ordered path, every vertex dated to the sol it was driven on, drives and waypoints indexed against it, and sourced moments merged. The coordinates are the mission's own.
datum: Mars 2000 sphere, radius 3,396,190 m; the service carries no elevations
note: The mapped ground path is 7.08 km. NASA gives 7.73 km, which is wheel odometry and includes the months Spirit spent turning in place at Troy with a dead wheel.

moments.title: Touchdown in Gusev Crater
moments.text: The lander hit at about 14 m/s, bounced 28 times and rolled 250 to 300 m to a stop, 13.4 km from its aim point. The site was named Columbia Memorial Station for the shuttle crew lost in 2003.

moments.title: Six wheels in the dirt
moments.text: Spirit drove off its lander platform onto Martian soil, 3 m in 78 seconds, finishing at 08:41 UTC. "We have six wheels in the dirt," said JPL director Charles Elachi.

moments.title: Sol 18: Spirit stops making sense
moments.text: The morning downlink cut out early and the rover began answering some commands and not others. A design error in a bundled DOS file system library had put it into a reset loop it could not shut down out of.

moments.title: The crippled mode command
moments.text: A hardware command that boots the rover without its flash file system broke the loop, with Opportunity due to land within twelve hours. Reeves and Neilson: "Without this capability, the MER mission may well have been lost."

moments.title: The first rock brushed on Mars
moments.text: With the flash memory reformatted and Spirit cleared for science again, the rock abrasion tool brushed dust off part of the rock Adirondack for five minutes. NASA called it the first interplanetary brushing of a rock.

moments.title: The first hole ground into a Martian rock
moments.text: The rock abrasion tool cut history's first grind into a rock on Mars, on Adirondack. The afternoon relay through Mars Odyssey came back with images of a round, clean-surfaced depression.

moments.title: On the rim of Bonneville
moments.text: The previous sol's drive had put Spirit at the rim of Bonneville crater. Spirit spent sol 67 manoeuvring into position to look inside and shoot a 360 degree panorama, putting 24.8 m on the odometer.

moments.title: Ninety sols, and the mission is complete
moments.text: Finishing 90 sols of surface operations met the last of the official success criteria for the prime mission. Two days earlier a 50.2 m drive had taken the total past the 600 m distance goal.

moments.title: Reaching the Columbia Hills
moments.text: After crossing more than 3 km of the Gusev plain, Spirit roved 42 m closer to a vantage point where it could study the outcrops of the Columbia Hills.

moments.title: A record hole in Clovis
moments.text: The rock abrasion tool ground for 2.5 hours into a brushed spot called Plano on the Clovis outcrop, cutting 8.9 mm, a record depth. Clovis was the most altered rock Spirit had met.

moments.title: Goethite, a mineral that needs water
moments.text: Spirit began a 48 hour Mossbauer reading inside the Clovis hole. NASA announced on 13 December 2004 that West Spur bedrock holds goethite, which "forms only in the presence of water, whether in liquid, ice or gaseous form".

moments.title: A wind cleans the solar panels
moments.text: Accumulated dust was blown off Spirit's solar arrays. Output climbed past 600 watt-hours on this sol, past 700 on the next and later past 800, about twice the level before the cleaning.

moments.title: The true summit of Husband Hill
moments.text: Spirit reached the true summit, at the eastern end of the nearly level crest it had gained in late August. The summit stands 106 m above the landing site. By the end of sol 618 it had driven 4,973 m.

moments.title: Salt in the soil at Arad
moments.text: Instruments on the robotic arm found that the white soil target Arad has a salty chemistry dominated by iron-bearing sulfates. NASA called the presence of salt another clue to the existence of past water on Mars.

moments.title: Home Plate
moments.text: Spirit reached the layered plateau it had first seen from the summit, 848 m of driving in 94 sols to get there, and perched at a 27 degree tilt to work on a rock target called Barnhill.

moments.title: The right front wheel stops
moments.text: The right front drive actuator stalled during a turn and ended the sol's 29 m drive. From here Spirit drove on five wheels, mostly backwards, dragging the dead sixth through the soil.

moments.title: Parked at Low Ridge Haven
moments.text: With winter closing in and an impassable sandy patch blocking the way to McCool Hill, Spirit settled on a 10.8 degree north-facing slope. The tilt bought 50 to 60 watt-hours a sol, about an hour of daytime science.

moments.title: The dragged wheel turns up white soil
moments.text: Spirit drove 1.9 m to a patch of bright soil that one of its wheels had churned up while being dragged. The team nicknamed it Gertrude Weise, and the mast spectrometer suggested it was rich in silica.

moments.title: Nearly pure silica
moments.text: NASA announced that the spectrometer on Spirit's arm had measured about 90 per cent pure silica in the Gertrude Weise soil. Steve Squyres: "You could hear people gasp in astonishment."

moments.title: The darkest sky: tau 4.738
moments.text: At the height of a planet-scale dust storm Spirit measured an atmospheric opacity of 4.738, a record for the rover, and its solar arrays fell to a matching record low of 261 watt-hours.

moments.title: On top of Home Plate
moments.text: Driving backwards to drag the frozen wheel, Spirit threaded between two rocks and put its rear wheels on the eastern edge of Home Plate, the plateau it had stayed off since sol 774.

moments.title: Difficult ground west of Home Plate
moments.text: Four drive sols, 1886, 1889, 1891 and 1892, gained about 3 m between them. NASA reported the terrain on the west side of Home Plate as very difficult and the rover as achieving very limited progress.

moments.title: Embedded
moments.text: A left wheel motor stalled during the sol's rover motion, and no motion was commanded for months. Spirit sat embedded in loose, soft terrain at a place called Troy, at risk of resting on a small mound of rocks under its belly.

moments.title: A second wheel gives out
moments.text: An extrication drive ended when the right rear wheel stalled after 1.4 m of wheel motion. An earlier stall on sol 1837, well before the embedding, suggested the cause could be internal to the wheel motor and gearbox.

moments.title: The last movement
moments.text: Spirit was commanded to flatten the suspension on its right side and lift it on the left, to tilt the solar panels north for the winter. Very little change in tilt was achieved.

moments.title: The last downlink
moments.text: Spirit was still under master sequence control with all systems green, making 134 watt-hours a sol, its power amplifier at a record low of minus 41.5 C. Odometry stood at 7,730.50 m. Nothing answered again.
